decisions.summary: Cedros Login remains the sole owner of user identity, authentication, mutable session validity, organization membership and role, and Login authorization policy.

Customer extensions use auth-response, host user-context, or public JWKS; specialized introspection and directory callers require explicit service authentication, scopes, audience policy, and organization allowlists.

TOTP seeds, OIDC client secrets, signing material, and service tokens live only in the per-extension host secret seam; database fields remain solely for one-way compatibility migration of legacy ciphertext.
The Login team-directory host service is organization-scoped and delegates password recovery through Login without granting system-wide user administration to an organization manager.

Preserve Login membership/team account management, wallet identifiers, invite grants, and account onboarding. Core owns site permissions and Team/Vault shell; Pay owns subscriptions, checkout, and discount application. Declare Pay >=3.0.2 as optional and keep configured gate failures closed. Data organization wildcards apply only to membership reauthorization, never directory/profile scopes.

Allow public native clients to register only http://localhost:PORT/callback with an explicit canonical port from 1 to 65535. Preserve HTTPS issuer, consent, resources, exact redirect matching and existing clients.

Preserve installed Login 2.0.19 native OAuth fixes; coalesce last-used metadata within one minute and reconcile only typed CAS precondition conflicts with bounded rereads, preserving current authority and metadata.
Preserve all five AI capability IDs and schemas; use executable extension-prefixed paths and validate the exact owning Wasm route before packaging.

surfaces.notes: Wasm routes and jobs own authentication, sessions, identity, organization authorization, and relying-party contracts.
Login-owned settings and identity administration remain under Extension Settings.
Public auth pages, blocks, and account workspace consume Login server contracts.
Package exports are present; runtime binding still requires the Cedros mobile host.
Login-owned metadata uses declared database models; credentials use the secret seam.
Published user-context, auth-response, JWKS, introspection, directory, and identity-profile seams.
The deterministic intake archive builds and validates locally.

evidence.details: Native Wasm-backend suite: 474 passed, 1 ignored. After final policy-binding and subscription changes, 25 relying-party tests and 4 subscription tests passed across focused reruns. These host-seam fixtures do not establish installed-host behavior.

evidence.details: All 19 affected UI contract tests passed across focused runs. UI typecheck, affected-file ESLint, and Prettier checks passed.

evidence.source: make cedros-validate plus focused reruns of repaired shell/readiness and remaining validators
evidence.details: All constituent repository validators passed after repairing dependency assertions and missing membership-route coverage. Database-concurrency evidence is model-only: 50 vectors; installed-host concurrency remains unverified.
No archive was rebuilt for this source audit; the prior artifact checksum no longer establishes evidence for the changed source.

Current kit 0.1.82: manifest schema, documentation consistency, and context schema pass. Runtime alignment fails because the compiled component is absent; final ZIP verification is unverified because no archive was built.

40 focused OAuth tests passed, including native authorization/consent/code exchange, S256 PKCE, exact redirect/resource binding and one-use codes. Full versioned ZIP build, Wasm ABI, archive and canonical authoring validation passed.
Coalescing boundary, newer timestamps, current metadata, race reconciliation, revocation, authority changes, bounded retries and non-precondition failure propagation.
All three route tests passed; verified keys require current membership, verified unsuspended owner, unexpired key and current revision; invalid shape is denied without storage access.
All five owned bindings pass; unprefixed, foreign, missing and mismatched routes fail before packaging.
Canonical package build, Wasm ABI, runtime exports, browser admin and immutable ZIP validation passed. No dependency changes.

unresolvedQuestions.question: Have mutable-session introspection, directory tenant isolation, legacy credential migration, and deletion cleanup passed against an installed Cedros host with configured secrets and database seams?
Has the Cedros mobile host bound and device-tested the packaged Login native provider and login screen?

How should relying-party token/policy updates commit atomically? Signing/HMAC initialization and signing-key rotation now use immutable encrypted secret versions selected by published database CAS. Separate relying-party token/policy secret writes can still partially commit. New relying-party policy/token bindings now deny access on a partial update rather than grant the old token the new policy. The authoring guide names extension.configuration.compare-and-set but the downloaded 0.1.82 conditional-operation registry does not specify its wire schema or a Login grant.

conflicts.resolution: Cedros authoring kit 0.1.82 publishes the Login contracts used by this repository, including cedros-data:abuse-budget-consume-v1; repository manifest and package metadata remain authoritative for the released Login 1.0.23 package identity.
